stories.title: India plans four rocket launch pads by 2029
stories.teaser: More launch pads mean more rockets, and more chances to explore space.

Std 7–8.headline: India plans four rocket launch pads by 2029
in_3_lines: ISRO, India's space agency, says India will have four working rocket launch pads by 2029.
Today India launches its big rockets from two pads at Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh.
More pads mean ISRO can launch more often, so more satellites, moon missions and maybe more astronauts.

why_explainers.question: Why does India need more launch pads?
why_explainers.answer: A rocket takes weeks to prepare on its pad. With only two pads, rockets wait in a queue, like students waiting for one computer in the lab. More pads let ISRO prepare several rockets at the same time and launch more often.

why_explainers.question: Why build a new launch site in Tamil Nadu?
why_explainers.answer: Some satellites must travel south over the poles. From Sriharikota, rockets going south must curve around Sri Lanka, which wastes fuel. A site at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu lets small rockets fly straight south over the sea.

backstory.point: India launched its first rocket from Thumba in Kerala. Parts were famously carried on a bicycle!
The Sriharikota launch centre opened. It is now called the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole after launching from Sriharikota.
ISRO's chief says four launch pads will be ready by 2029.

key_people.name: V. Narayanan
key_people.role: Head of ISRO, India's space agency
key_people.why_they_matter: He announced the plan and leads the people building India's rockets.

key_people.name: ISRO
key_people.why_they_matter: It builds and launches India's rockets and satellites, including the ones behind your phone's maps.

key_people.name: Launch pad
key_people.role: The platform a rocket stands on while it is prepared and launched
key_people.why_they_matter: Each pad can handle one rocket at a time, so the number of pads limits how often India can launch.

side_stories.point: Gaganyaan, India's mission to send astronauts to space, will need a busy and reliable launch schedule.
Private Indian companies are now building rockets too, and they also need places to launch from.

fun_facts.point: Sriharikota is an island between a lake and the sea, a safe spot to launch rockets out over the water.
Launching closer to the equator gives rockets a free push from Earth's spin, which saves fuel.

quiz.question: How many working launch pads does ISRO plan to have by 2029?
quiz.why: ISRO's chief said India will have four launch pads by 2029.

quiz.question: Where does India launch its big rockets from today?
quiz.why: Today's two pads are at Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh.

quiz.question: Why do more launch pads help?
options: ISRO can prepare and launch more rockets
quiz.why: Each rocket needs weeks on its pad, so more pads mean more launches.
